creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc compares Micron (MU) and Intel (INTC) as semiconductor stocks sell off despite booming earnings, sales and demand. Intel is expected to deliver 75% earnings-per-share growth a year for the next several years — its highest estimates in many years — as agentic AI lifts demand for CPUs, where Intel is a top-three data-centre player, even though it has no competitive GPU. Micron's EPS growth estimates peaked at 175% earlier in 2026 and have come back to 55%. The key difference is the source of growth: Intel's comes from selling more units, while Micron's comes from soaring memory prices — up triple digits in some quarters — on severe shortages, with supply sold out through 2027 and 2028 almost sold out. Micron has posted quarterly operating margins above 80% in its last two quarters, the highest he has seen in nearly a decade of coverage, and return on invested capital of 89% versus Intel at minus 7%. Intel's foundry business still lacks third-party customers and has spare capacity, keeping margins compressed, and its heavy manufacturing investment has expanded its capital base. On valuation, Intel trades at nearly 10x Micron's forward P/E; Micron is at just 3.3x. His DCF puts Intel fairly valued at $50 versus $54, and Micron at $1,539 versus $691. He owns Micron, not Intel. Calls: MU BUY at about $691, INTC AVOID at about $54 — a flip from HOLD.
